Verdict

No confirmed signs of a malicious supply-chain compromise. Overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

  • Use of OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, etc. appears to be normal single documented credential handling for LLM providers. No evidence of broad environment-variable scraping, secret discovery, or exfiltration was identified.
  • base64.b64decode appears to process message/file payload data. It is not paired with executable payload loading such as eval, exec, or compile.
  • The pre-scan hit for subprocess.run(..., shell=True) appears related to user-driven Markdown/command handling in utils/markdown.py; no evidence ties it to install-time or import-time malicious execution.
  • Network URLs for OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Cloudflare, and Vercel appear to be normal LLM provider endpoints, not attacker-controlled C2, webhooks, paste/drop services, or upload endpoints.

Automatic Execution Paths

Based on the provided extracted text and manifest, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, malicious setup.py, PEP 517 build-hook abuse, or malicious import-time side effects.

The visible code defines normal package/provider functionality; no path was identified that automatically performs credential theft, exfiltration, or persistence during installation or interpreter startup.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential harvesting: no evidence. Only normal single-provider API key environment lookups were observed.
  • Archive staging/exfiltration: no evidence of tar/zip/gzip staging, temporary harvested archives, base64 packaging of collected secrets, or uploads.
  • Persistence: no evidence of systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile edits, or background persistence loops.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence involving Kubernetes service-account tokens, Docker socket access, cloud metadata, CI/GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection.
  • Obfuscation/loader behavior: base64 decoding is used for file data handling, but no evidence links it to hidden executable payload loading via eval, exec, marshal, pickle, or similar mechanisms.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

No malicious distribution-integrity anomalies were confirmed from the provided information, such as hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, typosquatting indicators, sudden suspicious dependency insertion, or wheel/sdist mismatch.

The included .gitignore is a common project file in source distributions and is not itself evidence of a malicious supply-chain attack.
